findings.citation: The thumbnail existence check (`store.exists`) is not isolated: if it throws, the whole run rejects with that error.
findings.description: No scenario makes store.exists throw. The oracle behaves this way, but every scenario uses the in-memory store, whose exists never throws.

findings.citation: a failure while reading, probing, resizing or writing one image (including setting its metadata) counts it `failed`
findings.description: Only a probe failure (IMG_04, corrupt) is exercised. No scenario makes get, resize, put or setMetadata fail. No scenario checks partial state after a failure.

findings.citation: `layoutCarousel(items, rowHeight)` keeps `name` and `type`, sets `height` to `rowHeight` (any input height is not used for it)
findings.description: The layout scenario's items carry a height only together with a width, and in those cases the expected rows are computed from them. No item has an input height that differs from rowHeight, so the clause that the input height is ignored is not isolated.

findings.citation: The thumbnail existence check (`store.exists`) is not isolated: if it throws, the whole run rejects with that error.
findings.description: No scenario makes store.exists throw, so the required whole-run rejection behavior is not verified.

findings.citation: a failure while reading, probing, resizing or writing one image (including setting its metadata) counts it `failed`, adds an error message naming the image, and processing continues.
findings.description: The failure scenario exercises only a probe failure; failures from store.get, resize, store.put, and store.setMetadata are not checked.
